translated_text: "For the United States, China's spy activities are undoubtedly the greatest threat. But unfortunately, successive US administrations have not taken adequate measures due to their consideration of relations with China." This is pointed out by James Andrew Lewis, a former US diplomat familiar with China's spy activities and senior adviser at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). ◇Related article Spy or democratic activist: Historian tossed about between the US and China New York's Chinatown: China's " front line of spy activities" According to Lewis, China's spy activities are roughly divided into traditional human intelligence operations, so-called "HUMINT," and cyber-based operations. "Cross-border repression," in which China monitors or harasses democratic activists abroad, is also often carried out through human agents. Regarding China's spy activities in the US, Lewis explains, "When I conducted an investigation based on publicly available information a few years ago, China was twice as active as Russia."
